questions.text: Before sawing, the board is unstable and rocks on the workbench. What should be done?

options.text: Hold the board with your knee and saw with your free hand.
Have a colleague hold the board close to the cutting line.
Securely secure the workpiece with stops or clamps and only then begin sawing.
Start with short, quick movements so that the board itself takes a stable position.

questions.text: When sawing by hand, the cutting line runs close to the supporting hand. How to change work?

options.text: Rearrange and secure the workpiece so that the hand is outside the line of movement of the saw.
Increase the cutting speed to get through the dangerous area faster.
Turn the blade with the teeth in the opposite direction.
Continue, pressing the workpiece harder with your palm.

questions.text: A carpenter is planing a board and directing the plane toward the body. How should the technique be corrected?

options.text: Work with one hand and hold the blade with the other.
Continue moving towards yourself, but reduce the pressure.
Remove the stop from the workbench to allow the board to move.
Secure the board and guide the tool in a controlled manner away from the body along a stable path.

questions.text: The jigsaw blade is stuck in the workpiece. What is the first safe action?

options.text: Pull the tool towards you while the engine is running.
Release the switch, turn off the power and wait until the equipment stops completely.
Press the workpiece with your foot and increase the speed.
Try to release the blade with a screwdriver without turning off the power.

questions.text: How to check the suitability of the blade before installing it on the saw?

options.text: Install any disk with a suitable mounting hole.
Test the disc by hitting it on a metal workbench.
Check the type, size and permissible speed with the tool and make sure there is no damage.
Select a disc only by the color of the packaging.

questions.text: Sanding produces a lot of fine wood dust. Which measure is most effective?

options.text: Close the ventilation openings to prevent dust from flying around.
Use only cotton gloves.
Use a fan to move the dust into the common passage.
Apply dust removal at source, ventilation and risk-matched PPE.

questions.text: When is it permissible to change the saw blade or blade?

options.text: After disconnecting the tool from the power source and stopping all moving parts completely.
Idling at minimum speed.
Immediately after the switch is released, while the disk is rotating by inertia.
When the tool is turned on, if you use thick gloves.

questions.text: What is the correct sequence for pre-shift checking of power tools?

options.text: Check only the switch, without inspecting the equipment.
Remove the guard, turn on the tool and then check the disc by hand.
Inspect the housing and cable, check guards and accessories, then perform the specified no-load test.
First make a working cut, then inspect the cable and casing.

questions.text: How to shut down a power tool?

options.text: Leave the tool connected for the next shift.
Turn off, wait until it stops completely, turn off the power, clean and put away the tool.
Place the rotary tool on the workbench and turn it off later.
Stop the equipment by hand using a rag.

questions.text: What does kickback mean when using a saw?

options.text: Planned engine stop after the switch is released.
Gradual dulling of the cutting edge.
Normal removal of sawdust from a cut.
Sudden uncontrolled movement of the tool or workpiece due to jamming or catching of the disk.

questions.text: In the aisle near the workplace there are scraps and a power tool cable. What to do before starting work?

options.text: Cover the scraps with a sheet of plywood and begin work.
Remove any cuttings, route the cable safely and ensure clear passage.
Move the cable closer to the cutting line so that it is more visible.
Leave everything in place if the job takes less than an hour.

questions.text: On a circular saw, the protective guard does not return completely. What should a carpenter do?

options.text: Use the saw only for shallow cuts.
Lock the cover in the open position for convenience.
Lubricate the housing while rotating the disc and continue working.
Turn off the saw, take it out of service and report the malfunction.

questions.text: The handle of the chisel is split. What should I do?

options.text: Remove the tool from use until the handle is replaced or properly repaired.
Wrap the split with electrical tape and use for light work.
Hold the chisel by the metal part.
Use only a soft mallet without changing the handle.

questions.text: worker received an electric shock from a tool. What should an eyewitness do?

options.text: Pour water over the instrument to stop sparking.
First, put the tool in the cabinet, then inform the manager.
Safely turn off power, call for help and administer first aid without direct contact with live parts.
Grab the victim by the arms and pull him away.

questions.text: The insulation on the power tool cable is damaged. Which solution meets security requirements?

options.text: Connect the tool via a longer extension cord without repair.
Do not use the tool until the fault has been repaired in an authorized manner.
Cover the damage with paper and work in a dry room.
Hold the cable with your foot so that the damaged area does not move.

questions.text: Why are loose gloves dangerous around rotating equipment?

options.text: Gloves are sure to increase engine temperature.
Gloves change the direction of rotation of the tool.
Gloves interfere with work only at low temperatures.
The glove material may be caught by the rotating part and tighten the hand.

questions.text: How to properly store hand-held cutting tools after cleaning?

options.text: In a general pile with fasteners and scraps.
In a damp rag so that the metal does not heat up.
In a dry place, with the cutting part protected and without the risk of falling.
On the edge of the workbench with the cutting part facing out.

questions.text: What is the most efficient procedure for checking hand tools?

options.text: Check the tool’s intended use, the integrity of its handle, the condition of the working part and whether it is securely fastened.
Sharpen any tool, regardless of its purpose.
First test the tool with a maximum blow to the metal.
Only check that the handle is clean.

questions.text: The tool began vibrating strongly and produced an overheating smell. What is the correct sequence of actions?

options.text: Increase the load to reduce vibration.
Cool the instrument with water without switching off.
Continue until complete failure, then replace the equipment.
Immediately stop, disconnect, indicate fault and submit for inspection.

questions.text: What is the purpose of a tool guard?

options.text: Replace training and other protective measures.
Restrict access to hazardous moving parts and keep particle release within specified limits.
Hold the workpiece instead of the clamping device.
Increase the rotation speed of the equipment.

questions.text: Upon inspection of a piece of wood, a protruding nail was discovered. Which action is correct?

options.text: Do not start processing until the metal inclusion has been removed or the workpiece has been replaced.
Wear thicker gloves and process the workpiece in the usual way.
Process the area at minimum speed without changing the equipment.
Mark the nail with chalk and continue sawing next to it.

questions.text: A small part is difficult to hold when processing with a power tool. Which method is safer?

options.text: Hold the part with your fingers as close to the processing area as possible.
Press the part to the floor with shoes.
Secure the part with a suitable device and keep your hands out of the danger zone.
Ask a colleague to hold the part with his hand from the side of the tool exit.

questions.text: After planing, there were shavings left on the workbench near the cutting tool. How to remove it?

options.text: Blow the chips onto a colleague with compressed air.
After stopping and safely placing the tool, remove the chips with a brush or other tool.
Remove chips only after the end of the shift, without stopping work.
Brush the shavings with your palm towards the passage.

questions.text: Smoke and a burning smell appeared in the wood processing area. How to proceed?

options.text: Open all containers with flammable materials for inspection.
Close the room and continue work in the adjacent area.
Wait for visible flames without reporting signs of fire.
Stop work, turn off power when safe, sound the alarm, notify 101/112 and evacuate as appropriate.

questions.text: The worker is obstructed by the standard guard of the cutting part. What is acceptable?

options.text: Remove the guard for one cut and install it after work.
Secure the fence with wire in the open position.
Keep the guard in good condition and select a safe way to perform the operation according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Ask a colleague to hold the guardrail with his hand.

questions.text: High noise and flying chips are present at the same time. How to choose protection?

options.text: Wear proper eye and hearing protection appropriate to the risk assessment and the operation being performed.
Close your eyes when passing chips and do not use PPE.
Put on regular glasses and turn off the standard guard.
Select hearing protection only, as noise is more dangerous than wood chips.

questions.text: How to safely remove dust from tools after use?

options.text: Clean the ventilation holes with a metal wire while the power is on.
Blow the working tool with compressed air towards colleagues.
Immerse power tools in water.
Disconnect the tool and clean it in the manner specified in the instructions, without directing the contamination towards people.

questions.text: What should you check before starting to process a workpiece?

options.text: Only the availability of an unused socket.
Workplace, material and its fastening, serviceability of the tool and required protective measures.
Only the appearance of the finished product.
Only the execution speed of the previous operation.

questions.text: How to safely replace accessories?

options.text: Turn off the power, check the compatibility and condition of the equipment, install it according to the instructions and restore the fences.
Use any equipment of the same color.
After installation, immediately operate at full load without testing.
Remove the guard with the engine running and quickly replace the equipment.

questions.text: What is local dust removal?

options.text: Closing all air inlets during operation.
Cleaning the floor at the end of the shift with a dry broom.
Capture contamination directly at the point of its formation before spreading throughout the work area.
Dust is moved by a fan into an adjacent room.
